diagnostic_evidence.quote: a weighted $\lfloor t/2\rfloor$-design curve $\alpha=(\alpha_\Bbb R,\alpha_\Bbb C)$ on $S^2\subset\Bbb R\times\Bbb C$ satisfying $\alpha_\Bbb R(s)\neq-1$ for $s\in[0,1]$
$\alpha_3(s)=\sqrt{1-\alpha_1(s)^2}\sin(\pi\lfloor 2ts\rfloor/t+\theta_1(\alpha_1(s)))$
assuming $\theta_1(0)\neq m\pi-2n\pi/t$ for all $m,n\in\Bbb Z$, we may observe that setting $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)=w_{V_{2t},e^{i\theta(s)}}$, $\alpha_3(s)\neq-1$ for all $s\in[0,1]$

issues.failure_explanation: The lift of Theorem \ref{thm:S3stitch} requires the first coordinate of the base curve to avoid $-1$. Here $\alpha_3(s)=\sqrt{1-\alpha_1(s)^2}\sin(\pi j/t+\theta_1(\alpha_1(s)))$ takes the value $-1$ exactly at mid-segment parameters $s=(2j+1)/(4t)$ (where $\alpha_1=0$, so $\sqrt{1-\alpha_1^2}=1$) whenever $\theta_1(0)\equiv-\pi/2-j\pi/t \pmod{2\pi}$. The hypothesis in the theorem excludes instead the set $\{m\pi-2n\pi/t\}$, a different set: e.g. for $t=1$ and the admissible constant map $\theta_1\equiv\pi/2$ one gets $\alpha_3(3/4)=-1$, so formula \eqref{eq:explicitweight3} contains the division $1/\sqrt{1+\alpha_3(r)}=1/0$ and defines no curve. The stated hypothesis is thus insufficient (and also excludes harmless values such as $\theta_1(0)\equiv0$).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the excluded set by the true singular set, i.e. assume $\theta_1(0)\not\equiv-\pi/2-j\pi/t \pmod{2\pi}$ for all integers $j$ (and drop the unnecessary exclusions); the lift then applies verbatim and every other claim stands.
issues.overall_effect: For admissible $\theta_1$ (e.g. constant $\theta_1\equiv\pi/2$ at $t=1$) the advertised explicit weighted $(4t-1)$-design curve on $S^3$ in \eqref{eq:explicitweight3} is singular/undefined, so the $d=3$ part of Theorem \ref{thm:weight} fails as stated.
issues.title: Wrong singularity-avoidance hypothesis for the d=3 explicit lift in Theorem thm:weight
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the excluded parameter set makes the construction well defined; the lift argument, the design property, and the length claims all go through unchanged.

As printed the coefficient is $4\pi t$, which is not an integer multiple; $r(1^-)\neq r(0)$, the phase factor $e^{2\pi is+i\theta_2(r)}$ does not return to its start, and the curve is not closed, hence not a weighted $(4t-1)$-design curve as claimed, and the asserted length formula $2\pi\sqrt{32t^4-8t^2+1}$ corresponds to neither the printed nor the corrected parametrization without recomputation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $4\pi t$ by $4t$ in $r:=4\pi ts-\lfloor 4\pi ts\rfloor$ so that \eqref{eq:explicitweight3} is exactly the lift of Theorem \ref{thm:S3stitch} with strength $4t-1$, and recompute/verify the stated length and equality claims for the corrected formula.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit $d=3$ formula of Theorem \ref{thm:weight} (weighted $(4t-1)$-design property, exact length/equality statement, simplicity claim) is unsupported as printed; the abstract's claim that explicit formulas for $d\in\{2,3\}$ are presented is affected for $d=3$. The existence results for $d=3$ survive via the (independently defective) general construction only after its own repair.
issues.title: Spurious factor of pi in the lift parameter of the d=3 formula (eq:explicitweight3)
issues.why_classification: The coefficient correction is forced, but the theorem simultaneously promises an exact length value and an equality case that must be re-derived for the repaired parametrization (a contained, nontrivial recomputation); the asymptotic content survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: note from work of Dillon \cite[Theorem 1.6]{Dillon24} that for each $t\in\Bbb N$, there exists a constant $D_t$ we may assume is even such that for any $d\in\Bbb N_+$, there exists a weighted $t$-design set on $S^d$ of size at most $D_td^{t-1}$

For $d>1$, $t\in\Bbb N$, a weighted $t$-design set $(X=\{x_i\}_{i=1}^{2N},\lambda)$ on $S^{d-1}$, and any smooth path $M:[-1,1]\to O(d)$ in the space of orthogonal transformations of $\Bbb R^d$, $w_{X,M}$ constructed as in Section \ref{sec:weight} is a weighted $t$-design curve on $S^d$

issues.failure_explanation: The construction \eqref{eq:weightconst} takes a weighted $t$-design set on $S^{d-1}$ and produces a curve on $S^d$. The proof invokes Dillon's weighted $t$-design sets on $S^d$ (rather than on $S^{d-1}$), so the resulting curve $w_{X,M}$ lives on $S^{d+1}$, not on $S^d$; the theorem is not proved by this argument. The length threshold also does not match the statement ($D>\pi D_t t^d$ versus $D\ge\pi D_t d^{t-1}$, with the wrong dependence: $t^d$ instead of $d^{t-1}$).

failure_location.quote: Then, for any $D>\pi D_tt^d$, we may pick smooth $M:[0,1]\to O(d)$ such that $w_{X,M}$ is a weighted $t$-design curve of length $D$ with self-intersections and singularities at exactly $|X|+1$ values in $[0,1]$, proving Theorem \ref{thm:weightstrength}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Invoke Dillon's result on $S^{d-1}$ (size $\le D_t(d-1)^{t-1}\le D_td^{t-1}$), apply the suspension construction to get curves on $S^d$, and align the threshold with the statement ($D\ge\pi D_t(d-1)^{t-1}$ suffices for $D\ge\pi D_t d^{t-1}$).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem \ref{thm:weightstrength} (existence of weighted $t$-design curves on $S^d$ of length $\pi D_t d^{t-1}$ for all large $D$) is unsupported by its proof; the related prose about lengths $\pi d$, $2\pi d$ of 2- and 3-design curves inherits the sloppiness.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem thm:weightstrength applies the suspension construction on the wrong sphere
issues.why_classification: Both fixes are local (correct dimension of the design set and the threshold constant); the theorem's statement and rates are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: whose preimages $h^{-1}(s)$ we equip with the standard spherical measure $\sigma$ normalized so that $\sigma(h^{-1}(s))=1$
$w_\Bbb R(s)=(-1)^i(2(s-\Lambda_{i-1})-1), \quad w_{\Bbb R^d}(s)=\sqrt{1-w_\Bbb R(s)^2}M(w_\Bbb R(s))x_i$

issues.failure_explanation:
With $\sigma(h^{-1}(s))=1$ (probability measure on each fiber) the final identity $ rac12\int_{-1}^1\int_{h^{-1}(s)}f\,d\sigma\,ds=\int_{S^d}f\,d\sigma$ is false for $d
eq2$: the marginal of the normalized spherical measure under $h(\omega)=\omega_1$ has density $p(s)=\frac{A(S^{d-1})}{A(S^d)}(1-s^2)^{(d-2)/2}$, which is constant $1/2$ only for $d=2$. Since the printed parametrization traverses each latitude interval linearly, the parameter measure pushes forward to $ rac12 ds\otimes ar\sigma_s$, which equals $\sigma_{S^d}$ only for $d=2$. Concrete counterexample: $d=3$, any $t\ge2$, $f(\omega)=\omega_1^2$: the curve gives $ rac12\int_{-1}^1s^2ds= rac13$ while $\int_{S^3}\omega_1^2\,d\sigma= rac14$. Hence $w_{X,M}$ is a weighted $t$-design curve only for $d=2$, and Theorem \ref{thm:weightconst} (stated for $d>1$) is false as constructed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reparametrize each segment so the latitude $w_\mathbb{R}(s)$ is distributed with density proportional to $(1-s^2)^{(d-2)/2}$ (the quantile of the beta-type marginal), then redo the computation; lengths (parametrization-invariant), tunability, and the singularity set $\{\Lambda_i\}$ are unchanged, and Theorems \ref{thm:weightconst}, \ref{thm:weight} ($d\ge4$) and \ref{thm:weightstrength} follow as before.
issues.overall_effect: The central weighted construction is invalid in dimensions $d\ge3$: Theorem \ref{thm:weightconst} fails, and with it the general-$d$ ($d\ge4$) part of Theorem \ref{thm:weight} and all of Theorem \ref{thm:weightstrength}; the abstract's claim of asymptotically optimal weighted $t$-design curves 'for all $d$' is unsupported (the $d=2$ explicit curve and the $d=3$ lift route are unaffected by this root).
issues.title: Incorrect coarea identity: the suspension curve is not a weighted design curve for d≠2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained reparametrization (standard coarea/beta-quantile change of variable) that preserves the construction's length, rates, and all advertised claims; no new proof architecture is needed and no advertised regime is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Defining 
\[D_t:=\sup_{y_1\in Y_t}\inf_{y_2\in Y_t\setminus\{y_1\}}d_{\Bbb{CP}^n}(y_1,y_2)\]
for $d_{\Bbb{CP}^n}$ the metric on $\Bbb{CP}^n$ as in \eqref{eq:cpndist}, we have $D_t\asymp1/t$ as $t\to\infty$.
considering the covering radius $\rho_t$ of $Y_t$, we can see that $W_t\leq (|Y_t|-1)\rho_t/4$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs an upper bound on $W_t=2\sum_e\ell(e)$ (twice the total weight of the minimal spanning tree) and asserts $W_t\le(|Y_t|-1)\rho_t/4$, where $\rho_t$ is the covering radius. No argument is given, and the inequality is generically false: for a well-distributed design the spanning-tree edges have length comparable to the covering radius, giving $W_t\approx2(|Y_t|-1)\rho_t$, a factor $\sim8$ larger than claimed. Moreover the proof then uses '$\rho_t\asymp1/t$' citing Proposition \ref{pro:covrad}, whose quantity $D_t$ is the maximal nearest-neighbor (separation) distance, not the covering radius; no covering-radius bound is established anywhere in the source. Hence the estimate $W_t\lesssim t^{2n-1}$, and with it the computations of $\ell(\gamma_t)$ and $\varepsilon_t$, are unestablished.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Establish the covering-type bound $D_t^{\mathrm{cov}}\asymp1/t$ for the $Q_t$-designs of Proposition \ref{pro:CPnasymp} (standard for such designs), use $W_t=2\sum_e\ell(e)\le C(|Y_t|-1)\rho_t$ with an explicit constant (e.g. $C=4$ via a doubling-space argument), and keep the asymptotic conclusions.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem \ref{thm:main} (both the length asymptotic $\ell(\gamma_t)\asymp t^{2n}$ and the error bound $\varepsilon_t=O(1/t)$) is unsupported as written; the downstream Theorem \ref{thm:even} and Remark \ref{rmk:MZ}, which consume these asymptotics, lose their support until the estimate is repaired.
issues.title: Unjustified (and generically false) bound on W_t in the proof of Theorem thm:main
issues.why_classification: A corrected dispersion/covering estimate for these designs is a routine, local input; with the constant fixed, both advertised asymptotics ($\ell\asymp t^{2n}$, $\varepsilon_t\lesssim1/t$) survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists a sequence $(\gamma_t)_{t=0}^\infty$ of simple $\varepsilon_t$-approximate $t$-design cycles on $S^{2n+1}$ satisfying $\ell(\gamma_t)\asymp t^{2n}$ and $\varepsilon_t\asymp1/t$ as $t\to\infty$.

we have that $W_t\lesssim t^{2n-1}$ as $t\to\infty$. Therefore, we have $\delta_t\lesssim1/t$ as $t\to\infty$, so $\ell(\gamma_t)\asymp t^{2n}$ and $\varepsilon_t\asymp t^{2n}/t^{2n+1}=1/t$ as $t\to\infty$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof defines $\varepsilon_t=W_t/(\pi|Y_t|)$ and only derives an upper bound: $W_t\lesssim t^{2n-1}$ gives $\varepsilon_t\lesssim1/t$. The two-sided asymptotic $\varepsilon_t\asymp1/t$ asserted in the theorem (and in the abstract and Remark \ref{rmk:MZ} via $\widetilde\varepsilon_p\asymp1/p$) requires a lower bound $\varepsilon_t\gtrsim1/t$ for the constructed curves, for which no argument is given; the constructed error bound could in principle be much smaller than the true error, and no mechanism forcing $\varepsilon_t$ to be of exact order $1/t$ is supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a matching lower bound for the constructed cycles (e.g. exhibit, for each $t$, a polynomial of degree $≤t$ whose averages along the added connecting arcs versus the omitted fiber pieces differ by $≳(W_t+\delta_t)/(2π|Y_t|)$), or weaken the statement to $\varepsilon_t=O(1/t)$ and adjust Theorem \ref{thm:even} and Remark \ref{rmk:MZ} accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The rate claim $\varepsilon_t\asymp1/t$ of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, the corresponding part of Theorem \ref{thm:even}, and Remark \ref{rmk:MZ}'s $\widetilde\varepsilon_p\asymp1/p$ (hence the Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund constants) are unsupported; only $\varepsilon_t\lesssim1/t$ is established.
issues.title: Theorem thm:main claims epsilon_t ~ 1/t but the proof only bounds the error above
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial lower-bound argument (or a limited weakening of the advertised rate, withdrawing the 'in which case $\varepsilon_t\asymp1/t$' promise and the $\widetilde\varepsilon_p\asymp1/p$ corollary) is needed; the existence and length results survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
$\int_L f\,ds&=\int_{\gamma|_l}f+\int_{L\setminus\gamma(l)}f\,ds+\int_{\gamma|_{[0,1]\setminus l}}f-\int_{\gamma|_{[0,1]\setminus l}}f \\
&=\int_\gamma f+\int_{L\setminus\gamma(l)}f\,ds-\int_{\gamma|_{[0,1]\setminus l}}f.$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's first identity equates the arc-length integral of $f$ over $L$ with $\int_{\gamma|_l}f$ plus the rest; this identifies the curve's speed-weighted integral over $l$ with the arc-length integral over the image $\gamma(l)$, which is valid only when $\gamma$ covers $\gamma([0,1])\cap L$ with unit multiplicity. Without such a hypothesis the lemma is false: let $L$ be a $P_t$-design manifold with $c=1/|L|$, $\varepsilon=0$, and let $\gamma$ traverse $L$ twice; then $l=[0,1]$, $\ell(\gamma|_l)=\ell(\gamma)=2|L|$, so $\varepsilon_\gamma=\varepsilon-c|L|=-1$, and for $f\equiv1$ the claimed inequality reads $|2\int_L f\,ds-\int f\,d\sigma|=1\le-1$, a contradiction.

failure_location.quote: and a continuous, piecewise smooth, closed curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to S^d$, where $s$ is the arc length measure on $L$. Defining $l:=\gamma^{-1}(\gamma([0,1])\cap L)$ and setting $\varepsilon_\gamma:=\varepsilon+c(|L|+\ell(\gamma)-2\ell(\gamma|_l))$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $\gamma$ parametrizes $\gamma([0,1])\cap L$ with unit multiplicity (injective on $l$ up to measure zero), which holds in the application to Theorem \ref{thm:const}; the proof then stands.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma \ref{lem:overlap} cannot hold for curves with retraced/multiply-covered parts as stated; its application inside Lemma \ref{lem:smooth} (where no simplicity is assumed) is unsound, while the application in Theorem \ref{thm:const} (simple $\gamma_Y$) is unaffected.
issues.title: Lemma lem:overlap is false for curves retracing parts of L (missing multiplicity hypothesis)
issues.why_classification: Adding the missing local hypothesis (which the applications already satisfy) preserves the lemma and all its uses with no substantive loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: take $S$ to be the (finite) set of $s\in[0,1]$ such that $\gamma(s)$ is not smooth

As $(\varepsilon+2\delta c,c)$-approximate $t$-design curves have finitely many self-intersection points, we may perform this same procedure taking $S$ to be these self-intersection points to ensure $\widetilde\gamma$ will be simple.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof is not a valid argument: $S$ is a finite set of parameter values, so $\ell(\gamma|_S)=0$, making the required '$\ell(\gamma|_S)=\delta/2$' impossible; '$S\subset\gamma(S)$' compares a subset of $[0,1]$ with a subset of $S^d$; smoothing 'any curve which coincides with $\gamma$ on $[0,1]\setminus S$' cannot change the curve on a neighborhood of the finitely many singular parameters, so no smoothing occurs; and the self-intersection removal step treats self-intersection points (points of $S^d$) as parameter sets and provides no construction. No step connects to Lemma \ref{lem:overlap} with identifiable sets, so the lemma's conclusions (smooth/simple surrogate with length $\ell+\delta$ and error $\varepsilon+2\delta c$) are unsupported.

failure_location.quote: Consider an open subset $\widetilde S\subset[0,1]$ such that $\ell(\gamma|_S)=\delta/2$ and $S\subset\gamma(S)$. We may then smooth $\gamma$ to any curve $\widetilde\gamma$ which coincides with $\gamma$ on $[0,1]\setminus S$ and satisfies $\ell(\widetilde\gamma|_{S})=\delta/2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair:
Rewrite the proof: replace $S$ by a small open neighborhood of the non-smooth parameters with $\ell(\gamma|_{\widetilde S})=\delta/2$, replace $\gamma$ there by a smooth interpolant with controlled length change, apply Lemma \ref{lem:overlap} with $L$ the original image and $\gamma$ the modified curve, and (for simplicity, $d
eq2$) use a generic small perturbation off the self-intersections; the stated conclusions then follow.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma \ref{lem:smooth} is unproven; consequently the paper's claims that Theorems \ref{thm:const} and \ref{thm:main} also hold with smooth (and, for $d\neq2$, simple) curves in place of cycles are unsupported.
issues.title: Proof of Lemma lem:smooth is ill-posed and establishes nothing
issues.why_classification: The result is standard and its conclusions plausible, but a complete repair requires a contained, genuinely nontrivial smoothing-and-multiplicity bookkeeping argument (the current text proves nothing); no global re-architecture or loss of rates is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theorem \ref{thm:even} then directly follows from combining Proposition \ref{pro:caps} with Theorem \ref{thm:main}.

There exists a sequence $(\gamma_t)_{t=0}^\infty$ of $\varepsilon_t$-approximate $t$-design curves on $S^d$ of asymptotic order $\ell(\gamma_t)\asymp t^{d-1}\ell(\alpha_t)$ of arc length as $t\to\infty$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof obtains the even-dimensional curves solely by applying Proposition \ref{pro:caps} (the Ehler–Gröchenig cap construction) to the cycles of Theorem \ref{thm:main}. Neither the cited proposition nor its stated extension addresses simplicity of the resulting curves (the cap construction traverses many caps and traveling arcs and is not simple as stated), and the paper's own Lemma \ref{lem:smooth} only removes self-intersections for $d\neq2$ and is itself unproven. Hence the word 'simple' in Theorem \ref{thm:even} is not established.

failure_location.quote: For any $n\in\Bbb N$, there exists a sequence $(\gamma_t)_{t=0}^\infty$ of simple $\varepsilon_t$-approximate $t$-design curves on $S^{2n}$ satisfying $\varepsilon_t\asymp 1/t$ and $\ell(\gamma_t)\asymp t^{4n-3}$ as $t\to\infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either include an argument that the cap construction can be taken simple (e.g. via a corrected small-perturbation argument as in Lemma \ref{lem:smooth} for $d\ge4$) or delete 'simple' from the statement of Theorem \ref{thm:even}.
issues.overall_effect: The simplicity assertion in Theorem \ref{thm:even} (and any use of it) is unsupported; the existence and the rates $\varepsilon_t\asymp1/t$, $\ell\asymp t^{4n-3}$ are unaffected as claims.
issues.title: Theorem thm:even claims simple curves but its proof establishes none
issues.why_classification: Dropping the simplicity qualifier (or supplying a routine generic-position argument) leaves the theorem's substance and rates intact; no rate or regime is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Defining $l:=\gamma^{-1}(\gamma([0,1])\cap L)$ and setting $\varepsilon_\gamma:=\varepsilon+c(|L|+\ell(\gamma)-2\ell(\gamma|_l))$

issues.failure_explanation: In the displayed identity, $\int_{\gamma|_l}f$ (the curve's $|\gamma'|$-weighted integral over $l$) is silently identified with the arc-length integral of $f$ over the subset $\gamma(l)\subset L$. These agree only if $\gamma$ covers $\gamma([0,1])\cap L$ exactly once; with multiplicity $k\ge2$ the left side over-counts and the conclusion fails (e.g. $\gamma$ traversing an exact $t$-design manifold $L$ twice gives a negative claimed error $\varepsilon_\gamma=\varepsilon-c|L|$ while the actual error for $f\equiv1$ is $|c\ell(\gamma)-1|=1$).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $\gamma|_l$ is injective up to measure zero (satisfied by the simple cycle in Theorem \ref{thm:const}), so that $\int_{\gamma|_l}f=\int_{\gamma(l)}f\,ds$ and the computation is valid.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's guarantee is false without a unit-multiplicity/simplicity hypothesis on $\gamma$; uses of the lemma outside simple settings (as in the proof sketch of Lemma \ref{lem:smooth}, where $\gamma$ is an arbitrary approximate design curve) are unreliable.
issues.title: Lemma lem:overlap's derivation conflates parametrized and arc-length integrals
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard hypothesis under which the proof is valid preserves all applications (Theorem \ref{thm:const} uses a simple $\gamma_Y$); no substantive claim or rate is lost.
